title: 18.965 Geometry of Manifolds
description: Graduate first course on differentiable manifolds: charts and atlases, smooth maps and the standard pathologies, the derivative in Banach spaces, inverse and implicit function theorems, vector bundles and the tangent bundle, connections, partitions of unity, embedding theorems, Sard's theorem, fibre bundles, a linear-analysis interlude (Fredholm operators, Smale's Sard theorem), transversality, the strong Whitney embedding theorem, the Lie derivative, Frobenius and foliations, differential forms, Čech and de Rham cohomology and the de Rham theorem. Per-lecture outline notes (PDF) for 35 sessions in 26 files, plus six problem sets.
rightsNotes: Content is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 by MIT OpenCourseWare (footer licence link on every page opened); attribution and share-alike are required and commercial use is excluded. Corniversity is private and non-commercial.

Importing the lecture-notes PDFs for personal study and citation is within the licence. The course's problem sets are linked, not copied; any Corniversity exercise derived from them would be labelled adapted_with_attribution (none is at present).

The syllabus lists Bott–Tu, Abraham–Marsden–Ratiu and Hirsch as textbooks; those books are commercial and are not recorded as sources. The lecture notes are self-contained outlines and are the only material Corniversity cites.

syllabus: two 1.5-hour lectures per week; prerequisites Analysis II (18.101) and Algebraic Topology (18.905); grading 100% assignments; topic list (Banach manifolds and the inverse/implicit function theorems, Sard and parametric transversality, Whitney embedding, Pontryagin–Thom and Freudenthal, Morse theory, differential forms and de Rham, Smale's immersion theorem); textbooks Bott–Tu, Abraham–Marsden–Ratiu, Hirsch
calendar: 35 sessions with topics; no dates or milestones
lecture notes page: 26 PDF resources covering sessions 1–35 (sessions 10–11, 16–17, 18–19, 21–22 and 23–28 share files)
assignments page: six problem sets listed as resource pages (not opened)

every lecture PDF: downloaded and text-extracted on 2026-10-30; none carries printed page labels; files are 1–9 pages each; the lectures 23–28 file is a one-page handout stating that no notes are provided for those lectures
limitations: The notes are terse lecture outlines (often 1–4 pages per lecture) with many proofs left as exercises; Corniversity lessons supply the missing detail and cite the notes for statements.

No lecture PDF has printed page labels; the physical page index is the only page reference. Printed running numbers appear in the page footers of some files (e.g. lecture 1 pages 1–4) and are not recorded as labels.
Problem-set PDFs were listed on the assignments page but not opened; no locators exist for them.
Despite the landing-page description, the calendar and notes contain no lectures on Riemannian metrics; the Riemannian material of this catalogue is sourced elsewhere (see MAT-262).
Lectures 23–28 (Morse theory) have no notes beyond a one-page definition handout, so no Corniversity unit relies on them.
Text extraction of these PDFs garbles some mathematical symbols; statement numbers and page indices were checked against the extracted text, not against rendered pages.
